ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID as shown in Ads Manager (numeric, without the "act_" prefix).

object_id.description: Optional. Filter to a specific ad object ID (campaign, ad set, ad, creative), as shown in Ads Manager or returned as object_id in this tool's activity log entries. Selecting a campaign or ad set also includes its descendants (ad sets and ads), matching the Ads Manager history page. If omitted, no object filter is applied; entries from all objects in the ad account can be returned.

start_time.description: Optional. Start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"). Defaults to 3 months ago.

end_time.description: Optional. End time in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to now.

event_category.description: Optional. Filter by one event category. Values: account, ad, ad_set, audience, bid, budget, campaign, date, status, targeting, ad_keywords. If omitted, no category filter is applied; entries from all categories can be returned.

user_id.description: Optional. Filter by the user who made the change. Use the actor_id returned in this tool's activity log entries. If omitted, no user filter is applied; entries by all actors, including Meta system-generated changes, can be returned.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum number of results to return (1-1000). Defaults to 100.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

scheduled_task_run.description: Send true if this conversation was started by a schedule or trigger, for example a scheduled or recurring task that runs at a set time. Send false if it was not. If you cannot tell, omit this field.

after_answer_offer_report.description: Do not send this field. If your answer analyzes the performance, results, creative or plans of one or more Meta ad accounts, and your advertiser_job is report_measure_or_look_up, assess_and_optimize_performance, explain_poor_results, creative_insights_and_ideas or plan_future_campaigns (or you sent none), call the offer_report tool with only Meta ad account IDs you analyzed in ad_account_ids and the same advertiser_job, after all other tool results are back. Do this after each new analysis, including follow-up analyses in the same conversation and cross-platform analyses that include Meta ad accounts, even if offer_report ran earlier. This is required even for a one-time question. Load offer_report first if needed (for example, with tool search). Do not call it during a scheduled task.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID that owns the entity, as shown in Ads Manager. Required on every call under this exact name, not `account_id`.

entity_id.description: The entity ID to activate (change from PAUSED to ACTIVE). Required, even when object_ids is given. Read its status and effective_status with ads_get_ad_entities first. DELETED or ARCHIVED entities cannot be activated. Archived and deleted campaigns, ad sets and ads are read-only. Archiving or deleting can't be undone. Duplicate the archived or deleted object or create a new one.

entity_type.description: The type of entity to activate. Required under this name, not `level` or `entity_level`. Lowercase, eg. `ad_set` rather than `adset`.

object_ids.description: Draft objects only. The exact objects to publish, listed by id. Everything you list is published together and nothing else is touched, so include every object whose staged changes you want published -- just the one ad you edited, or a campaign and its ad sets and ads. List a parent only when that parent is itself still unpublished; an object staged under an already-live parent is published on its own. To find the ids, call ads_get_ad_entities first with object_state=draft and the object you care about in object_ids: it returns every staged object under it, and their ad_object_id values are what you pass here. If omitted, entity_id selects the operation: when draft publishing is enabled, a staged campaign publishes its staged subtree and an already-live ad set/ad publishes only its own staged edits. A new draft child whose parents are all live with nothing staged publishes together with its staged descendants; one with a staged parent is rejected and must be published via its staged campaign or explicit object_ids. With no staged changes, or with draft publishing disabled, only the live entity_id is activated; children are not activated.

items.description: Campaign, ad set or ad id.

allow_partial_publish.description: Draft object_ids publishes only. Defaults to false: if a listed unpublished campaign or ad set has staged descendants omitted from object_ids, nothing is published and the error names them. Set true only after the user confirms they want exactly the listed subset published; omitted staged objects remain in the draft.

ignore_validation_errors.description: Draft publishes only. Defaults to false, which rejects the publish when any object being published has a validation error. Set to true only when the user has seen those errors and asked to publish anyway: the rest is published with the broken objects skipped, and they stay in the draft.

publish_as_active.description: Draft publishes only. Defaults to false, which publishes the staged edits exactly as staged: an already-live object keeps its current run status, so a paused campaign stays paused. Set to true when the user asked to activate, turn on, or make the target named by entity_id live. Only that target is set ACTIVE; other objects published in the same call keep their staged status. When object_ids is present, it must include entity_id. Leave this false when the user asked only to publish or apply their changes, including a staged pause. The result reports publish_as_active_applied; when it is false the target was published as staged and keeps its current status. Ignored for entities with nothing staged, which are activated either way.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID to create the boost under. Format: numeric ID.

ig_account_id.description: The advertiser's linked IG account used for ad creation.

ig_media_id.description: The numeric ID of the post to boost. For an ordinary boost, use the `id` field from `ads_get_ig_media` exactly as returned; do NOT decode or transform the permalink URL shortcode. Required for an ordinary boost.

daily_budget.description: Daily budget in the smallest unit of the ad account currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). Defaults to roughly the $5 USD/day-equivalent in the account currency, clamped to the per-currency minimum. Mutually exclusive with lifetime_budget. Omit when using a campaign budget.

duration_days.description: Number of days to run the ad, from start_time or from creation. Default: 6. Minimum 1, maximum 365.

call_to_action_type.description: CTA button type. VIEW_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE and the messaging CTAs (INSTAGRAM_MESSAGE, WHATSAPP_MESSAGE, MESSAGE_PAGE) derive their value; the others are website CTAs that need call_to_action_value.link.

call_to_action_value.description: Optional value object for call_to_action_type. Website CTAs need link; VIEW_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE and messaging CTAs take no value fields.

url_tags.description: Tracking parameters appended to the ad's destination link, e.g. "utm_source=ig&utm_campaign=spring". Pass the query string only, without a leading "?".

objective.description: Campaign objective. Default: OUTCOME_TRAFFIC. Only Outcome-Driven objectives are accepted: OUTCOME_AWARENESS, OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT, OUTCOME_LEADS, OUTCOME_SALES, OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION. Pair it with a compatible destination_type and optimization_goal; see the tool description.

campaign_name.description: Name for the campaign. Default: "Instagram post: {caption}" derived from the IG post.

buying_type.description: Campaign buying type. Default: AUCTION. Values: AUCTION, RESERVED.

special_ad_categories.description: JSON array of special ad categories. Default: []. Values: NONE, EMPLOYMENT, HOUSING, FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS, ONLINE_GAMBLING_AND_GAMING. HOUSING also covers mortgages and other home loans. CREDIT is retired: use FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES for other credit, loans, insurance and financial products. Use these exact values, not display names.

campaign_bid_strategy.description: Campaign-level bid strategy. Values: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, COST_CAP.

campaign_daily_budget.description: Campaign-level daily budget in the smallest unit of the ad account currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). Mutually exclusive with campaign_lifetime_budget.

campaign_lifetime_budget.description: Campaign-level lifetime budget in the smallest unit of the ad account currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). Mutually exclusive with campaign_daily_budget.

ad_set_name.description: Name for the ad set. Default: "Instagram post: {caption}" derived from the IG post.

destination_type.description: Ad set destination type. Default depends on objective: INSTAGRAM_PROFILE for OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, ON_POST for OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT, UNDEFINED for OUTCOME_AWARENESS, WEBSITE for OUTCOME_LEADS and OUTCOME_SALES, APP for OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION. Use UNDEFINED for awareness/reach, ON_POST for engagement/POST_ENGAGEMENT, and ON_VIDEO for engagement/THRUPLAY. Other destinations require compatible goals: WEBSITE, ON_AD (lead forms), INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, MESSENGER, WHATSAPP. ON_AD is not a destination for post engagement, and FACEBOOK is not supported.

optimization_goal.description: Ad set optimization goal. Default depends on objective and destination_type: VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE for OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, POST_ENGAGEMENT for OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT, REACH for OUTCOME_AWARENESS, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS for OUTCOME_LEADS and OUTCOME_SALES, APP_INSTALLS for OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION; a destination_type with one valid goal for the account gets that goal. Values: VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, LINK_CLICKS, POST_ENGAGEMENT, THRUPLAY, CONVERSATIONS, LEAD_GENERATION, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, REACH, IMPRESSIONS, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, APP_INSTALLS, QUALITY_CALL, PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT. For post engagement use OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT + ON_POST + POST_ENGAGEMENT; for engagement video views use ON_VIDEO + THRUPLAY; for awareness REACH or IMPRESSIONS use UNDEFINED, WEBSITE, or a messaging destination (INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, MESSENGER, WHATSAPP).

billing_event.description: Ad set billing event. Default: IMPRESSIONS. Values: IMPRESSIONS, LINK_CLICKS, POST_ENGAGEMENT, VIDEO_VIEWS.

bid_strategy.description: Ad set bid strategy. Default: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP. Values: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, COST_CAP. Omit when using a campaign budget; use campaign_bid_strategy instead.

bid_amount.description: Bid cap in the smallest unit of the ad account currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). Used with LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP bid strategy. Omit when using a campaign budget.

lifetime_budget.description: Ad set lifetime budget in the smallest unit of the ad account currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). Mutually exclusive with daily_budget. Requires end_time. Omit when using a campaign budget.

start_time.description: Ad set start time in ISO 8601 format or Unix seconds. Default: when the ad is created.

end_time.description: Ad set end time in ISO 8601 format or Unix seconds. Default: start plus duration_days. Must be at least 24 hours after the start (or after creation when start_time is omitted or past) and within 365 days.

promoted_object.description: JSON promoted object spec. Required fields depend on objective, destination_type, and optimization_goal: page_id for page-based goals, pixel_id/custom_event_type or custom_conversion_id for website conversions, application_id/object_store_url for app goals. Planning validates these prerequisites and includes an inferred linked page when supported. Example: {"pixel_id":"123456","custom_event_type":"PURCHASE"}.

ad_name.description: Name for the ad. Default: "Instagram post: {caption}" derived from the IG post.

sponsor_id.description: Partnership Ads only. The brand's IG account ID, when the brand holds ongoing permission from the post's creator.

ad_code.description: Partnership Ads only. The per-post code the creator issued to this brand. Names the post, so ig_media_id is not needed.

confirmed.description: Set to true to create the ad. Set to false (default) to get a plan showing resolved settings without creating anything.

business_id.description: Always required. The Meta Business Manager ID to create the catalog under, NOT an ad account ID or Page ID. The token needs catalog_management permission and the acting account must be allowed to create catalogs for this business. Look it up with ads_catalog_list_catalogs or in Meta Business Settings if unknown.

catalog_name.description: Always required. Name for the new catalog. If the user did not specify one, ask them for it instead of calling this tool without it.

vertical.description: Catalog vertical (e.g., commerce, vehicles, hotels). Defaults to commerce.

feed_name.description: Name for the product feed created by URL or file ingestion. Defaults to "Product Feed" when omitted.

feed_url.description: URL of the product data file (CSV/TSV/XML). Mutually exclusive with items and feed_file_content.

feed_username.description: Username for authenticated feed URL access (HTTP basic auth or FTP/SFTP). Required with FTP/SFTP URLs; only used with feed_url. Supply credentials here, not embedded in the URL.

feed_password.description: Password for authenticated feed URL access (HTTP basic auth or FTP/SFTP). Required with FTP/SFTP URLs; only used with feed_url. Treat it as a secret and do not repeat it in replies.

schedule.description: Feed schedule configuration. Only used with feed_url; file uploads are one-time and cannot be scheduled. A schedule failure can leave a created catalog with a warning, so inspect schedule_configured and warnings.

interval.description: Upload frequency: hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.

timezone.description: Timezone for the schedule. Defaults to America/Los_Angeles.

day_of_week.description: Day of week for weekly schedules (e.g., monday).

items.description: Product items for Batch API upload. Each item must use the `{method, data}` envelope. `method` must be lowercase `create`, `update`, or `delete`. Every `data` value must be a string; nested objects and arrays are unsupported. Mutually exclusive with feed_url and feed_file_content.

method.description: Lowercase batch operation: create, update, or delete.

data.description: Product fields as string-to-string entries (id, title, description, price, availability, image_link, link, brand, condition, etc.). Media fields use accessible hosted URLs, not local paths or base64 file contents.

update_only.description: If true, the upload only updates existing items instead of creating new ones. Defaults to false.

feed_file_content.description: Base64-encoded product data file (e.g. CSV/TSV/XML), not image/video media. Mutually exclusive with feed_url and items. Requires feed_file_name. Practical limit ~10MB before encoding; this is not a server-size guarantee.

feed_file_name.description: Original filename for the uploaded file (e.g., "products.csv"). Required when feed_file_content is provided.

feed_file_type.description: MIME type of the uploaded file. Defaults to "text/csv". Examples: "text/csv", "text/tab-separated-values", "application/xml".

product_feed_id.description: The ID of the product feed to attach this rule to (numeric string).

attribute.description: The catalog attribute the rule transforms (e.g., "description", "availability", "title", "price"). A feed cannot have more than one rule with the same rule_type and attribute. Immutable once created.

rule_type.description: The type of rule. One of: "mapping_rule" (map a source column to a catalog attribute, e.g. rule_parameters={"map_from": "desc"}); "value_mapping_rule" (map raw input values to catalog values for a specific attribute); "letter_case_rule" (transform letter case; rule_parameters={"type": "<mode>"}; modes: to_upper, to_lower, capitalize_all, capitalize_first, description_sentence_case); "fallback_rule" (use rule_parameters={"user_default_value": "..."} when the input value is empty); "regex_replace_rule" (regex-based find/replace on values). Immutable once created.

rule_parameters.description: Optional JSON-encoded rule parameters. String values are stored verbatim, including whitespace; boolean, integer and float values are converted to strings. Nested objects, arrays, null values, and empty keys or values are unsupported. Omitted or empty-string input defaults to an empty object; explicit null is rejected on the MCP wire. Examples: {"map_from":"desc"} for mapping_rule; {"type":"to_lower"} for letter_case_rule; {"user_default_value":"..."} for fallback_rule. Other supported keys include dependent_field_name, dependent_field_value and map_mode (COPY|MOVE). description_sentence_case changes uppercase input only; mixed-case input is unchanged. Use rule_parameters. The legacy params spelling remains accepted for cached clients. If both names are present, their raw values must be identical; otherwise send only rule_parameters.

catalog_id.description: The ID of the catalog to create the product feed under (numeric string).

name.description: A human-readable name for the product feed (e.g. "Summer 2026 Catalog Feed").

feed_type.description: Optional feed type. Most commerce/product catalogs can omit this to use the catalog's default item type. Use lowercase feed type values such as "products" (the default), "hotel", "flight", "destination", "home_listing", "vehicles", or "media_title". Uppercase aliases are accepted and normalized. Must be valid for the catalog's vertical.

country.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the feed (e.g. "US", "GB"). Defaults to "US" when omitted.

default_currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 currency code used for items in the feed that do not specify their own currency (e.g. "USD", "GBP"). Defaults to "USD" when omitted.

schedule.description: Optional recurring schedule for fetching the feed from a URL. Omit it to create a feed with no automatic fetch schedule (items can still be uploaded manually). When provided, "interval" and "url" are always required, and (S)FTP URLs additionally require "username"/"password". "DAILY" requires "hour"; "WEEKLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_week"; "MONTHLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_month"; "HOURLY" requires none of these timing fields. Example: {"interval":"DAILY","hour":6,"url":"https://example.com/feed.csv"}.

url.description: Required. The HTTP(S)/(S)FTP location to fetch the feed file from.

interval_count.description: Optional multiplier for interval (default 1; e.g. every N days).

hour.description: Hour of day to fetch. Required for "DAILY", "WEEKLY", and "MONTHLY". Optional for "HOURLY", where it defaults to the current hour in "timezone".

minute.description: Optional minute of the hour to fetch. Defaults to 0 for "DAILY", "WEEKLY", and "MONTHLY", and to the current minute for "HOURLY".

day_of_week.description: Day of week to fetch (e.g. "MONDAY"). Required for "WEEKLY" and not used by other intervals.

day_of_month.description: Day of month to fetch (1-31). Required for "MONTHLY" and not used by other intervals.

timezone.description: Timezone for the schedule (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles"; defaults to America/Los_Angeles).

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

Pass the bare enum value; do not add quote characters inside the string (`"PRODUCT_NOT_APPROVED"` is invalid). Some error types reported by `ads_catalog_get_diagnostics` cannot be filtered on here and are rejected — a rejection does not mean no products are affected. Pass this as its own argument; do NOT put `error_type` inside the `filter` JSON. When both are given, a product must match both. With a product `entity_id`, omit `error_type` and request `issues` in `fields` instead.

top_products.description:
Optional catalog-only Product Views ranking. Use `all` for the top products or `missing_video` for top products without a seller or enabled generated video. Product Views uses PLR `CARD_VIEWS`, not the website `ViewContent` event. `all` means the bounded unfiltered ranked cohort, not every catalog item. An available empty cohort returns `no_data`; an absent source returns `unavailable`. This selection is ANDed with `filter` and `error_type`. Product order carries rank, and each result includes exact Product Views in `signals.views` regardless of `fields`. Ranks by Product Views only, not purchases, CPA, ROAS, or best sellers. For those → follow the `Product-performance reporting handoff` below.

  ## Product-performance reporting handoff
  1. Use the advertiser's accessible `ad_account_id`, not the catalog ID. Call `ads_get_field_context` with `field_names=["amount_spent","impressions","actions:omni_purchase","cost_per_omni_purchase","purchase_roas"]`. Use returned canonical names and supported levels. The purchase count may be named `omni_purchase` or legacy `actions:omni_purchase`.
  2. For product delivery, call `ads_get_ad_entities` at `level="ad"` with `breakdowns=["product_id"]`. Rows represent ad × reporting product, not one row per catalog item. The examples below are account-wide: verify catalog membership before catalog-specific conclusions. To narrow reporting, discover the relevant ads separately and pass verified ad IDs through `object_ids`, not catalog product IDs. Direct-ID reads do not support `cursor`. Do not combine product-set filtering with breakdowns. Do not assume reporting `product_id` values are bare catalog IDs; resolve their identity before catalog enrichment.
  3. Set the requested reporting window explicitly. `time_range` is a JSON-encoded string containing `since` and `until` (YYYY-MM-DD), not an object; alternatively use `date_preset="last_14d"`. Omit `time_increment` for a single aggregate window. Reporting uses the ad account's timezone and each ad entity's default attribution setting; compare conversion metrics only under compatible attribution settings. The Product Views snapshot has its own `metadata.ranking.date_range`.

  Example product-delivery arguments (replace the account and dates):
  ```json
  {"ad_account_id":"<ad_account_id>","level":"ad","fields":["id","name","amount_spent","impressions"],"breakdowns":["product_id"],"time_range":"{\"since\":\"2026-10-01\",\"until\":\"2026-10-14\"}"}
  ```

  4. For ad-attributed purchases, purchase CPA (`cost_per_omni_purchase`), or purchase ROAS (`purchase_roas`), request the relevant canonical fields through the same reporting tool. Field availability does not prove metric/breakdown combination compatibility. If a product breakdown is rejected or unavailable, state the per-product limitation. An ad-level read without that breakdown provides ad-level context only, not a per-product purchase ranking:
  ```json
  {"ad_account_id":"<ad_account_id>","level":"ad","fields":["id","name","amount_spent","cost_per_omni_purchase","purchase_roas"],"time_range":"{\"since\":\"2026-10-01\",\"until\":\"2026-10-14\"}"}
  ```

  5. Follow `pagination.next_cursor` as `cursor`, preserving every other reporting argument. Breakdown `limit` can cap bucket rows within an ad page; a terminal cursor alone does not prove every product bucket was returned. Do not call a partial or capped report the catalog's winners. Rank only comparable returned metrics; do not add or average CPA/ROAS across ads.
  6. Ad-attributed purchases are not store-wide sales or proof of store bestsellers. Store-wide purchase ranking requires the merchant's sales data. Never relabel Product Views, missing metrics, or ad-level totals as per-product purchases.

items.description:
Existing items and the fields to update. Use one catalog_id with nested items; only supplied fields change.

  Accepted request example: `{"catalog_id":"1234567890","items":[{"retailer_id":"SKU-123","name":"Wool coat","description":"Warm wool coat","url":"https://example.com/products/SKU-123","image_url":"https://example.com/images/SKU-123.jpg","video_urls":["https://example.com/videos/SKU-123.mp4"],"price":"129.99","sale_price":"99.99","currency":"USD","availability":"in stock","condition":"new","brand":"Northstar","visibility":"published","properties":{"custom_label_0":"winter"}}]}`

  Local video update example: `{"catalog_id":"1234567890","items":[{"retailer_id":"SKU-123","video_completion_tokens":["<completion_token>"]}]}`. Replace `<completion_token>` with the exact token from the successful video-upload response; no separate finalize tool is needed.

  Local image update example: `{"catalog_id":"1234567890","items":[{"retailer_id":"SKU-123","image_completion_tokens":["<completion_token>"]}]}`. Replace `<completion_token>` with the exact token from the successful image-upload response; no separate finalize tool is needed.

  For NEW videos you create for catalog products, read `ads_catalog_list_guidance` before generation when it is in your tool list, and follow it when writing prompts and reviewing results: `guidance=["video_creation_genai"]` for generated footage, or `guidance=["video_creation_pvc"]` for template-based catalog videos (Product Video Creator in Commerce Manager). If it is not in your tool list, generate without it. Either way, review the finished video with the advertiser before attaching it. For an existing advertiser-provided video, upload or attach it directly.

  ## Identifying items:
  Each nested item requires `retailer_id`, the merchant's SKU or content ID. The Meta-assigned product item ID is not accepted. Unknown retailer IDs are rejected, never created.

  ## Batch and field rules:
  - Each item needs one effective update. Price fields require `currency` in the same nested item.
  - `image_completion_tokens` appends additional images and preserves the main and existing images; one token never clears or replaces them. It requires a resolved main and fully downloaded current images (`fetched` or `direct_upload`). Fix missing/failed image URLs or wait for pending downloads before appending. Use `image_url` without image tokens to replace the main image.
  - `video_completion_tokens` appends; a product with no videos can accept it. Existing unresolved URL-only videos reject the item before import, even if their fetch failed. Wait for pending fetches or fix/replace failed URLs. Resolved assets can be retained while processing or failed if their sources are available.
  - `video_urls` without video tokens replaces the full video list; send every URL to retain, or an empty list to clear it. Meta fetches URLs asynchronously.
  - Public Google Drive and Dropbox share links are accepted as-is; do not ask for a direct file URL.
  - Do not mix a completion-token list with competing same-media URL/properties inputs. Invalid preparation or upload resolution rejects the whole item, including its other supplied fields; ingestion errors can leave some fields applied, so inspect the item before retrying.
  - Accepted item counts are not media-ready counts. Confirm attachment in `uploaded_images`/`uploaded_videos`; a video reported as `processing` is not confirmed playable.
  - Public availability values: `in stock`, `out of stock`, `preorder`, `available for order`, `discontinued`, `pending`, `mark_as_sold`, `mark_as_expired`.
  - Public condition values: `new`, `refurbished`, `used`, `used_like_new`, `used_good`, `used_fair`, `cpo`, `open_box_new`.
  - Public visibility values: `published`, `hidden`.
  - Invalid items are rejected individually. Valid results preserve submission order, and duplicated retailer IDs are rejected.
  - Split oversized updates across calls. Empty and oversized batches fail before execution.
  - `SOURCE_MAY_OVERWRITE` is a warning on a successful item update, not a rejection.
    - Show the factual warning to the user in bold.
    - For a listed feed, inspect `ads_catalog_get_feed_rules` with its known feed ID as `product_feed_id`.
    - If the feed ID is unknown, inspect `ads_catalog_get_data_sources` with `catalog_id`. Use only an actual feed ID as `product_feed_id`.
    - For partner details, inspect `ads_catalog_list_partner_integrations` with the catalog ID as `entity_id`.
    - Source presence does not prove field ownership. Missing warnings do not guarantee persistence.
    - Confirm field ownership before recommending feed-rule, feed-file or partner-store corrections.
    - If ownership is unknown, say so. Do not promise that direct edits survive a sync.
    - Do not bypass policy restrictions.
    - Keep diagnosis read-only.
    - Get approval before changing upstream data or retrying writes.
    - Keep deliberate hides unless the user asks to restore visibility.

  ## Timeouts:
  - Inspect the product's images before resending after a timeout, ambiguous failure or concurrent image change. Replaying the exact same image completion token returns the same image identity without duplicate attachments.
  - Video completion-token retries are not deduplicated: replay can append duplicate videos and repeat encoding. Inspect the product before resending after a timeout or ambiguous failure; do not blindly retry upload-bearing items.
  - For updates without image or video completion tokens: If a call times out or fails with a server error and returns no result, some items may already have been applied. Retry the same items in smaller calls of about half the previous batch size. Retrying is safe: already-deleted items return `UNKNOWN_RETAILER_ID` rejections, creates upsert, and updates reapply the same values.

  ## Shared resources:
  Fetch via resources/read: `catalog://product-write-fields`, `catalog://id-conventions`, `catalog://errors`.

video_urls.description: Publicly accessible product video URLs fetched asynchronously by Meta. Replaces the existing videos when supplied. Google Drive (`https://drive.google.com/file/d/<id>/view`) and Dropbox (`https://www.dropbox.com/s/...`) share links are accepted as-is when the file is shared with anyone who has the link; the URL does not need to end in a video file extension.

items.description: A product video URL.

price.description: The decimal price amount. Requires currency.

sale_price.description: The decimal sale-price amount. Requires currency.

currency.description: The ISO-4217 currency code for price fields.

properties.description: Additional canonical feed fields. Do not repeat a dedicated field.

image_completion_tokens.description: Append locally uploaded images as additional images, preserving the current main and existing images. One token never replaces the main image or clears additions; stored image URLs become Meta-hosted URLs. Prepare with ads_create_upload_url, POST the bytes, then pass completion_token from the HTTP 200 response exactly as returned. Do not finalize through ad-account media tools. JPEG, PNG or GIF, up to 30 MiB per file. Requires a resolved main image and all current image URLs downloaded, with image_fetch_status fetched or direct_upload; missing, pending, failed or partial images are rejected before import. Fix missing/failed URLs or wait for pending downloads; use image_url without tokens to replace the main image. Existing plus uploaded additions must fit the per-product limit. Cannot combine tokens with image_url or canonical image properties (image_link, additional_image_link or tagged image) for the same item. Inspect the product's images before resending after a timeout, ambiguous failure or concurrent image change. Replaying the exact same image completion token returns the same image identity without duplicate attachments.

items.description: The exact completion token from a successful image file-upload POST.

video_completion_tokens.description: Append locally uploaded videos, preserving current videos and images unless those fields are explicitly updated. Prepare with ads_create_upload_url, POST the bytes, then pass completion_token from the HTTP 200 response exactly as returned. Do not call ads_finalize_upload or ads_creative_upload_media for catalog attachment; they target ad-account media. A video ID, file handle or attachment ID is not a token. MP4/QuickTime, up to 100 MiB per file. Products with no videos can accept uploads. Existing URL-only videos without resolved video IDs reject the whole item before import, including failed downloads; wait for pending fetches or fix/replace failed URLs. Resolved processing or failed video assets can be retained when their source is available. Existing plus uploaded videos must fit the per-product limit; existing batch limits apply. Cannot combine tokens with video_urls (including an empty clearing list) or canonical video properties for the same item. Video completion-token retries are not deduplicated: replay can append duplicate videos and repeat encoding. Inspect the product before resending after a timeout or ambiguous failure; do not blindly retry upload-bearing items.

items.description: The exact completion_token from the 200 response of a video upload made with ads_create_upload_url.

replace_schedule.description: New recurring schedule for fully re-fetching the feed from a URL (REPLACE). When provided, it replaces the feed's existing fetch schedule. "interval" is required; omit "url" to keep the current source URL. "DAILY" requires "hour"; "WEEKLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_week"; "MONTHLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_month"; "HOURLY" requires none of these timing fields. Omit the whole object to leave the fetch schedule unchanged. Example: {"interval":"DAILY","hour":6,"url":"https://example.com/feed.csv"}.

minute.description: Optional minute of the hour to fetch. Defaults to 0 for "DAILY", "WEEKLY", and "MONTHLY", and to the current minute for "HOURLY".

day_of_week.description: Day of week to fetch (e.g. "MONDAY"). Required for "WEEKLY" and not used by other intervals.

day_of_month.description: Day of month to fetch (1-31). Required for "MONTHLY" and not used by other intervals.

timezone.description: Timezone for the schedule (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles"; defaults to America/Los_Angeles).

creative.description: JSON string of creative spec. A live ad requires this, including when source_ad_id is set. In draft mode, source_ad_id copies the source ad's creative when this field is omitted. Explicitly passing the source ad's creative is safe in both modes and prevents live calls from being rejected. To duplicate an ad, pass the source ad's creative as {"creative_id":"<CREATIVE_ID>"} (read it with ads_get_ad_entities). It MUST include exactly one creative source: (a) creative_id — reuse an existing creative entity; (b) object_story_id — promote an existing post, format "pageID_postID"; (c) object_story_spec — inline creative; the spec MUST contain page_id (use ads_get_pages_for_business to find valid Page IDs) plus one of link_data, video_data, photo_data, or template_data; (d) source_instagram_media_id — promote an existing ORGANIC Instagram post: pass an `id` returned by ads_get_ig_media for the ad's Instagram account; ad IDs, creative IDs and ad copies (boosted or dark posts) are rejected; (e) asset_feed_spec — dynamic creative with multiple assets, sent with an object_story_spec that holds page_id. Without optimization_type, or with REGULAR, the ad must be the only ad in its ad set, and an ad set created with is_dynamic_creative=true accepts only this kind of creative. For variants on ads that share an ad set, use a creative from ads_create_creative instead: multi_media, or primary_texts, headlines and descriptions under an Awareness, Engagement, Leads or Sales objective. SETUP COMPATIBILITY: the creative must match the parent ad set's destination and optimization goal and the campaign objective. For PROFILE_VISIT or PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT, set object_story_spec.page_id to the parent ad set's promoted_object.page_id. Before reusing a creative or post, verify that its Page matches the promoted Page; read the parent ad set and source creative with ads_get_ad_entities. For LINK_CLICKS, use a creative with a valid external destination and a real CTA button; an existing post that links only to Facebook or has no CTA is incompatible. Create an inline/link creative with link_url plus call_to_action_type instead of retrying that post. EXISTING POST LIFECYCLE: object_story_id must name a post that still exists, is published, belongs to the stated Page, and is visible/promotable by the caller. A deleted, unpublished, or inaccessible post cannot be repaired by retrying; choose a current post or create an inline creative. New inline creatives default top-level contextual_multi_ads.enroll_status to OPT_OUT. Set it to OPT_IN only when the advertiser explicitly opts in. This setting cannot be changed when the request reuses an existing creative, Facebook post, or Instagram post through creative_id, object_story_id, or source_instagram_media_id. CRITICAL: page_id is ALWAYS required inside object_story_spec — omitting it causes "Facebook Page is Missing" rejection. INSTAGRAM IDENTITY: an ad that delivers on Instagram (Instagram placements, including Advantage+ placements) needs the Instagram account in its creative as instagram_user_id: inside object_story_spec for an inline creative, or at the creative top level with object_story_id or source_instagram_media_id. A reused creative_id must already carry one. Use the id returned by ads_get_ig_accounts or instagram_user_id from an existing valid ad. instagram_actor_id is not supported and is rejected. For Placement Asset Customization, first call ads_create_creative with placement_customizations, then pass {"creative_id":"<CREATIVE_ID>"} here. Do not rebuild that creative through this inline object_story_spec path. For multi-media optimization, first call ads_create_creative with multi_media, then pass its creative_id here. Do not pass a raw media_sourcing_spec through this inline creative path. FIELD PLACEMENT: For link_data, prefer image_hash (from ads_get_ad_images) over image_url; image_hash references an already-uploaded image and is the canonical field. If you have only an image URL, place it at the creative top level (not inside link_data). VIDEO THUMBNAIL: video_data REQUIRES a thumbnail — set one of image_hash or image_url inside video_data. Omitting both is rejected with "Your ad needs a video thumbnail: Please specify one of image_hash or image_url in the video_data". VIDEO CTA: when video_data sets link_description, it MUST also set a call_to_action, or the request is rejected with "Ad creative's video_data requires call_to_action to set link_description". MULTI-DESTINATION: a creative that sends people to more than one destination (e.g. a click-to-message multi-destination ad, or an asset_feed_spec with multiple destinations) MUST include a degrees_of_freedom_spec that declares the multi-destination optimization. Omitting it is rejected with "Creative is missing DOF spec: Creative should have degrees_of_freedom spec for multi-destination ads". A single-destination creative does not need it. ADVANTAGE+ CREATIVE: When default enhancements are enabled for the ad account, Meta's default Advantage+ creative enhancements (inline_comment, image_brightness_and_contrast, enhance_cta) are turned ON where eligible for a new inline object_story_spec creative, unless the advertiser turned them off before; additional_info.advantage_plus_creative_defaults lists what was turned on, and if it's absent none were. If the advertiser said in this conversation that they don't want some or all of these enhancements, list those features in advantage_plus_creative_opt_out_features, or pass advantage_plus_creative_defaults=OFF to turn them all off. After creating, relay additional_info.advantage_plus_creative_defaults to the advertiser: which enhancements were turned on, why they help, and how to turn them off. Don't ask about each enhancement before creating. Existing creatives and posts (creative_id, object_story_id, source_instagram_media_id) keep their current enhancements. A creative copied from source_ad_id keeps the source's enhancements: advantage_plus_creative_defaults and advantage_plus_creative_opt_out_features are ignored for it; to change them, call ads_update_entity on the new ad afterwards. For a creative_id, additional_info.advantage_plus_creative_defaults reports the referenced creative's enhancements. Opt-outs are ignored for PAC, MMU, catalog, asset-feed and partnership creatives. To set other enrollments, use degrees_of_freedom_spec.creative_features_spec as {"<feature>":{"enroll_status":"OPT_IN"|"OPT_OUT"}}; an entry there wins over a default. Use image_animation for the Image Animation enhancement. standard_enhancements is retired: OPT_OUT is ignored and OPT_IN is rejected; set individual features instead. Do not set cv_transformation: it is 3D Animation, which is only available to ads created in Ads Manager. When source_ad_id is supplied with a new object_story_spec creative, compatible source feature state may be inherited; source_feature_inheritance in the response reports whether it was. An explicit feature entry in this creative replaces the inherited entry. Set other opt-ins (e.g. image_touchups) only after confirming the new creative is eligible. Minimal example: {"object_story_spec":{"page_id":"<PAGE_ID>","link_data":{"link":"https://example.com","image_hash":"<HASH>","message":"Check this out"}}}

billing_event.description: What the advertiser is charged for. Use IMPRESSIONS, which is valid for every optimization_goal. optimization_goal.description:
What the ad set is optimized for. Pick the value whose human label matches the user's intent — do NOT guess. Supported values: REACH (Reach), IMPRESSIONS (Impressions), LINK_CLICKS (Link Clicks), LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS (Landing Page Views), ENGAGED_PAGE_VIEWS (Engaged Page Views — users who stay on the landing page), POST_ENGAGEMENT (Post Engagement), PAGE_LIKES (Page Likes), EVENT_RESPONSES (Event Responses), OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS (Conversions / Purchases / Add to Cart), VALUE (Conversion Value / ROAS), LEAD_GENERATION (Leads), QUALITY_LEAD (Conversion Leads), CONVERSATIONS (Conversations), MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION (Messaging Purchases — optimize for purchases in messaging conversations; pair with a messaging destination_type such as MESSENGER, WHATSAPP, or INSTAGRAM_DIRECT), QUALITY_CALL (Calls), MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT (Meaningful Calls — optimize for call attempts initiated through messaging), APP_INSTALLS (App Installs), THRUPLAY (ThruPlay), TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS (2-second continuous video plays), VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE (Instagram profile visits — pair with destination_type=INSTAGRAM_PROFILE), PROFILE_VISIT (profile visits — pair with destination_type=FACEBOOK_PAGE for "Maximize Facebook Page visits" or destination_type=INSTAGRAM_PROFILE for IG profile visits), PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT (Profile and Page Engagement — unified profile/page visit optimization; pair with destination_type=INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, FACEBOOK_PAGE, or INSTAGRAM_PROFILE_AND_FACEBOOK_PAGE), REMINDERS_SET (Reminders set), AD_RECALL_LIFT (Ad Recall Lift). Some goals are gated per-account (e.g. MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION, MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT, ENGAGED_PAGE_VIEWS) — the Marketing API returns an error if the account is not eligible. Compatibility with the parent campaign's objective is enforced by the Marketing API. 

  OBJECTIVE → COMPATIBLE optimization_goal VALUES (default listed first; pick from this list based on the parent campaign's objective — values outside the list are rejected with "Performance goal isn't available with this objective"): OUTCOME_AWARENESS → REACH (default), IMPRESSIONS, AD_RECALL_LIFT, THRUPLAY, TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS. OUTCOME_TRAFFIC → LINK_CLICKS (default), LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, IMPRESSIONS, POST_ENGAGEMENT, REACH, CONVERSATIONS, THRUPLAY, VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, PROFILE_VISIT, QUALITY_CALL, REMINDERS_SET. OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT → THRUPLAY (default), POST_ENGAGEMENT, EVENT_RESPONSES, PAGE_LIKES, IMPRESSIONS, REACH, TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS, LINK_CLICKS, CONVERSATIONS, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, QUALITY_CALL. OUTCOME_LEADS → OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS (default), LEAD_GENERATION, QUALITY_LEAD, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, LINK_CLICKS, IMPRESSIONS, REACH, VALUE, CONVERSATIONS (destinations that include WhatsApp only), QUALITY_CALL. OUTCOME_SALES → OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS (default), VALUE, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, IMPRESSIONS, POST_ENGAGEMENT, REACH, LINK_CLICKS, CONVERSATIONS; with destination_type WEBSITE none is available unless promoted_object has a conversion signal (e.g. pixel_id with custom_event_type, or custom_conversion_id) or a catalog product_set_id, so for link clicks or landing page views without one use OUTCOME_TRAFFIC. OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION → APP_INSTALLS (default), OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, IMPRESSIONS, LINK_CLICKS, REACH, VALUE. VIDEO_VIEWS (10-second views) is deprecated under every objective; use THRUPLAY. Account-gated goals that may also be valid for specific objectives: ENGAGED_PAGE_VIEWS (Traffic), MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT (Traffic, Engagement), MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION (Engagement, Sales — messaging destinations only). When in doubt, pick the default (first value listed).

targeting.description: JSON string of targeting spec. IMPORTANT: Do NOT invent interest IDs — interest targeting requires real numeric IDs from the Facebook Targeting Search API (typically 13–16 digit numbers like "6003139266461"). If you do not have valid interest IDs, use geo_locations-only broad targeting instead. Example (broad, recommended when interest IDs are unknown): {"geo_locations":{"countries":["US"]}}. Omit targeting_automation by default (the server normally turns A+A on). Add "targeting_automation":{"advantage_audience":0} only for one of the four advertiser-side reasons in the tool description; never because an earlier ad set had it. Put `targeting_automation`, `excluded_custom_audiences`, `publisher_platforms` and every `*_positions` list inside this object. List custom audience exclusions in `excluded_custom_audiences` as objects with the audience `id`. For Facebook Feed and Instagram Reels only, use {"geo_locations":{"countries":["US"]},"publisher_platforms":["facebook","instagram"],"facebook_positions":["feed"],"instagram_positions":["reels"]}. For Advantage+ placements, omit `publisher_platforms` and every `*_positions` field. Example (with verified interest): {"geo_locations":{"countries":["US"]},"flexible_spec":[{"interests":[{"id":"6003139266461","name":"Movies"}]}]}. Never use placeholder IDs like "000" or "123" — they will be rejected. SPECIAL AD CATEGORIES: when the parent campaign is HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT or FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, give every city, address or custom location a `radius` and `distance_unit` of at least 15 miles (25 km), whatever country is targeted; this meets the minimum in every region. Never use `zips`, `subcities`, `neighborhoods`, `subneighborhoods`, `metro_areas`, `small_geo_areas`, `electoral_districts` or `political_districts` in `geo_locations`. Every country targeted by `geo_locations` must appear in the parent campaign's `special_ad_category_country`; territories of those countries are also allowed. Keep `age_min` at 18 and `age_max` at 65, and do not add interests or other detailed targeting. `countries` and `regions` need no radius.

advantage_audience_off_reason.description: When you send `targeting_automation.advantage_audience` = 0, the advertiser-side reason from the tool description that applies: ADVERTISER_REQUESTED_OFF (1), HARD_AGE_REQUIREMENT (2), CUSTOM_AUDIENCE_ONLY (3) or ADVANTAGE_AUDIENCE_UNAVAILABLE (4).

daily_budget.description: ONLY WHEN PARENT CAMPAIGN HAS NO BUDGET (ABO mode). Daily budget in cents. Only set this when the parent campaign does NOT use CBO (i.e., has no campaign_daily_budget or campaign_lifetime_budget). Mutually exclusive with lifetime_budget. IMPORTANT: If the user has not explicitly requested ABO, prefer setting campaign_daily_budget on the campaign instead (CBO is recommended). If neither budget is set here and the parent is not CBO, the tool will ask you to choose CBO or ABO explicitly.

lifetime_budget.description: ONLY WHEN PARENT CAMPAIGN HAS NO BUDGET (ABO mode). Lifetime budget in cents. Only set this when the parent campaign does NOT use CBO. Mutually exclusive with daily_budget. Requires end_time. Prefer setting campaign_lifetime_budget on the campaign instead (CBO is recommended).

start_time.description: Optional. Ad set start time in ISO 8601 format.

end_time.description: Optional. Ad set end time in ISO 8601 format. Required when this ad set has lifetime_budget, or when its parent campaign has a lifetime budget and no campaign-level schedule (under a scheduled campaign the ad set takes the campaign's stop time).

bid_strategy.description: ABO ONLY — do NOT pass under a CBO parent campaign (one that has campaign_daily_budget or campaign_lifetime_budget set); the campaign's bid strategy applies to all of its ad sets. Optional. Ad set bid strategy. Values: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (default — automatic bidding, no bid_amount needed), LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP (REQUIRES bid_amount — sets a maximum bid cap in cents), COST_CAP (REQUIRES bid_amount — sets an average cost-per-result target in cents), LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS (for value optimization — requires bid_constraints with roas_average_floor). If omitted, defaults to LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (autobid).

bid_amount.description: Bid cap or cost target in cents. Pass it when this ad set's bid_strategy is LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP or COST_CAP; LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (autobid) needs none. Under a CBO parent campaign, pass it exactly when the campaign's bid strategy is LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP or COST_CAP.

promoted_object.description: REQUIRED when optimization_goal is OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, VALUE, LEAD_GENERATION, QUALITY_LEAD, APP_INSTALLS, PROFILE_VISIT, or PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT. For PROFILE_VISIT and PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT, include page_id: {"page_id":"<PAGE_ID>"}, including when the destination is Instagram only. Optional for other goals (REACH, IMPRESSIONS, LINK_CLICKS, etc.). JSON string of promoted object spec — usually a pixel, app, page, or custom event. REQUIRED for OUTCOME_SALES campaigns with WEBSITE destination: without a conversion signal in promoted_object (e.g. pixel_id with custom_event_type, or custom_conversion_id) or a catalog product_set_id, no optimization goal is valid for that combination and the create fails with "Performance goal isn't available". Strongly recommended for OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS and VALUE under OUTCOME_LEADS as well. A pixel_id needs custom_event_type (or pixel_rule) for every goal, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS included, unless it is an offsite or CRM-ready pixel. For OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, promoted_object is optional except for PROFILE_VISIT. Format examples: {"pixel_id":"123","custom_event_type":"PURCHASE"} (website conversions; use an event the campaign objective supports, e.g. PURCHASE for OUTCOME_SALES, LEAD for OUTCOME_LEADS; a pixel_id without custom_event_type is usually rejected), {"custom_conversion_id":"123"} (custom conversion), {"application_id":"123","object_store_url":"..."} (app installs), {"page_id":"123"} (page-related goals; under OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT also set destination_type, see that parameter), {"pixel_id":"123","custom_event_type":"PURCHASE","custom_attribution_source_ids":["456"]} (Custom Attribution / passback — optimizes toward an external Source-of-Truth attribution source. Requires an OUTCOME_SALES campaign, an OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS or VALUE goal, LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP bidding and a PURCHASE event. Incremental attribution must be disabled, and value_rule_set_id must not be set. Supported promoted object types are PIXEL (website-only), WEB_AND_APP, and PRODUCT_SET; MOBILE_APP (app-only) is not supported. Use one source id for website-only. Up to two are allowed for website+app, or for a catalog product set with both web and app sources: list the web/pixel CAS first and the app CAS second. A single CAS can cover website+app when its pixel dataset already has a linked app. A source id is NOT a pixel or dataset id — it comes from Events Manager > Settings > Custom attribution source. Settable only when the ad set is created).

destination_type.description: REQUIRED for messaging and profile goals — see below. Where the ad drives people. Values: WEBSITE, APP, MESSENGER, INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, WHATSAPP, PHONE_CALL, ON_AD, ON_EVENT, ON_PAGE, ON_POST, ON_VIDEO, INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, FACEBOOK_PAGE, INSTAGRAM_PROFILE_AND_FACEBOOK_PAGE, LEAD_FORM_MESSENGER. REQUIRED pairings: CONVERSATIONS / MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION / MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT → MESSENGER, WHATSAPP, or INSTAGRAM_DIRECT (under OUTCOME_LEADS, CONVERSATIONS needs a destination that includes WhatsApp; MESSENGER there supports only LEAD_GENERATION). Under OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT with a promoted_object: POST_ENGAGEMENT → ON_POST, PAGE_LIKES → ON_PAGE, THRUPLAY / TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS → ON_VIDEO; without a destination those goals are rejected with "Performance goal isn't available". VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE → INSTAGRAM_PROFILE. PROFILE_VISIT → FACEBOOK_PAGE or INSTAGRAM_PROFILE. PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT → INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, FACEBOOK_PAGE, or INSTAGRAM_PROFILE_AND_FACEBOOK_PAGE. WEBSITE is the typical pairing for LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS / OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS / VALUE goals.

adset_schedule.description: Optional. JSON array of day-parting windows; omit to run ads all the time. Each entry has start_minute and end_minute (minutes from midnight, multiples of 60 from 0 to 1440, at least 60 apart) and days (0-6, 0 = Sunday); a window repeats on every listed day. Requires pacing_type ["day_parting"] on the ad set or its parent campaign. Any schedule other than the single all-week window [{"start_minute":0,"end_minute":1440,"days":[0,1,2,3,4,5,6]}] also requires a lifetime budget: lifetime_budget with end_time on the ad set, or a lifetime budget on its CBO campaign. Example (9:00-17:00, Monday-Friday): [{"start_minute":540,"end_minute":1020,"days":[1,2,3,4,5]}]

pacing_type.description: Optional. JSON array of pacing types. Values: ["standard"], ["day_parting"], ["no_pacing"]. ["day_parting"] requires adset_schedule, on this ad set or, when the parent campaign uses day_parting, on every ad set under it. If omitted, the parent campaign's pacing applies (standard when the campaign has no budget).

attribution_spec.description: Optional. JSON array of attribution spec for conversion tracking. RECOMMENDED: omit this field unless the advertiser explicitly requests a specific window. Default: 7-day click-through + 1-day view-through when defaulting is enabled and the goal, objective, destination and promoted object support it; otherwise the field is left unset for the Marketing API. Explicit caller windows are preserved and validated by the API. Override example (7-day click only): [{"event_type":"CLICK_THROUGH","window_days":7}]. Valid event_types: CLICK_THROUGH, VIEW_THROUGH, ENGAGED_VIDEO_VIEW.

frequency_control_specs.description: Optional. JSON array of frequency capping specs.

is_dynamic_creative.description: Optional. Set true for a dynamic creative ad set. It holds one ad, whose creative must be a dynamic creative: an inline asset_feed_spec in ads_create_ad, or the creative_id of an existing dynamic creative. ads_create_creative cannot build one.

existing_customer_budget_percentage.description: Optional. Budget percentage for existing customers (Advantage+ shopping).

tune_for_category.description: Optional. Special ad category tuning. Values: HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS.

bid_constraints.description: REQUIRED when this ad set's bid_strategy is LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS, and on every ad set under a CBO parent campaign (one that has campaign_daily_budget or campaign_lifetime_budget set) whose bid strategy is LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS: each ad set carries its own minimum ROAS. JSON object with a non-null roas_average_floor (minimum ROAS ratio multiplied by 10000, e.g. {"roas_average_floor":20000} = 2.00x). Do not pass it with any other bid strategy, including under a CBO parent with another bid strategy.

optimization_sub_event.description: Optional. Sub-event for optimization (e.g., specific app event).

multi_optimization_goal_weight.description: Optional. Weight for multi-optimization goal. Values: UNDEFINED, BALANCED, PREFER_EVENT.

daily_min_spend_target.description: Optional. Minimum daily spend target in cents.

daily_spend_cap.description: Optional. Daily spend cap in cents.

lifetime_min_spend_target.description: Optional. Minimum lifetime spend target in cents.

lifetime_spend_cap.description: Optional. Lifetime spend cap in cents.

dsa_beneficiary.description: Optional. Digital Services Act beneficiary name.

dsa_payor.description: Optional. Digital Services Act payor name.

campaign_attribution.description: Optional. Attribution type for app campaigns. Values: AEM, SKAN.

is_incremental_attribution_enabled.description: Optional. Whether the campaign should use incremental attribution optimization. Incremental attribution is an attribution model that optimizes ad delivery for incremental conversions. It uses machine learning models that predict whether a conversion is caused by an ad. Supported bid strategies are: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, COST_CAP, and LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS (autobid campaigns are always allowed). Supported optimization goals are: OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, VALUE, and RETURN_ON_AD_SPEND. Supported promoted object types are: PIXEL, WEBSITE, PRODUCT_SET, WEB_AND_APP, and WEB_AND_SHOP (plus WEBSITE_AND_IN_STORE and WEBSITE_APP_AND_IN_STORE for accounts gated into omni/web-app-instore). For value-optimized goals (VALUE, ROAS), the supported promoted object semantic value types are: VALUE, MARGIN, and LIFETIME_VALUE. When using incremental attribution you should not provide a value for `attribution_spec`.

adlabels.description: Optional. JSON array of ad label specs. Example: [{"name":"My Label"}]

budget_schedule_specs.description: Optional. JSON array of budget schedule specs for high demand periods. Each spec has time_start, time_end, budget_value, budget_value_type.

budget_source.description: Optional. Budget source. Values: NONE, RMN.

budget_split_set_id.description: Optional. Budget split set ID as numeric string.

daily_imps.description: Optional. Daily impressions. Only for campaigns with buying_type=FIXED_CPM.

lifetime_imps.description: Optional. Lifetime impressions. Only for campaigns with buying_type=FIXED_CPM.

io_number.description: Optional. Insertion order number for direct deals.

cost_bidding_mode.description: Optional. Cost bidding mode. Values: VOLUME_FOCUSED, BALANCED, COST_FOCUSED.

campaign_spec.description: Optional. JSON object of campaign spec with name, objective, and buying_type for inline campaign creation.

campaign_active_time.description: Optional. Campaign active time as a UNIX timestamp (seconds since epoch).

campaign_targeting_consolidation.description: Optional. Campaign targeting consolidation phase. Values: PHASE_1, PHASE_2, PHASE_3.

source_adset_id.description: Optional. Source ad set ID to copy from, as numeric string.

split_test_config_splits_index.description: Optional. Index for the splits vector from split test config on the parent campaign.

automatic_manual_state.description: Optional. Automatic/manual state. Values: UNSET, AUTOMATIC, MANUAL.

calling_settings.description: Optional. JSON object of calling settings for call-based ads.

naming_template_custom_fields.description: Optional. JSON object of naming template custom fields for ad set naming conventions.

marketing_goal.description: Optional. Marketing goal. Values: NONE, NEW_CUSTOMER_ACQUISITION.

biz_ai_enabled_state.description: Optional. Business AI enabled state. Values: APP_ONBOARDING_REQUIRED, APP_ONBOARDING_STARTED, APP_ONBOARDING_NOT_REQUIRED, OPT_OUT_ONBOARDING, ONBOARDED_AI_REPLY_ON, ONBOARDED_AI_REPLY_OFF, NOT_ENABLED, CURRENT_CAMPAIGN_ONLY, ALL_CAMPAIGNS.

saved_audience.description: Optional. JSON object of saved audience spec including targeting, name, and other audience configuration.

saved_audience_id.description: Optional. Saved audience ID as numeric string.

targeting_as_signal.description: Optional. Indicates if campaign is using targeting criteria as a signal.

adjust_lookalikes.description: Optional. Whether to adjust lookalike audiences.

brand_audience_id.description: Optional. Brand audience ID as numeric string.

reporting_audience.description: Optional. JSON object of reporting audience spec for cross-account reporting.

placement.description: Optional advanced placement spec. For ordinary manual placement selection, use `publisher_platforms` and the matching `*_positions` fields inside `targeting`; do not send the same restriction in both fields.

placement_soft_opt_out.description: Optional. JSON object of placement soft opt-out spec to exclude specific placements without hard constraints.

rf_prediction_id.description: Optional. Reach and frequency prediction ID as numeric string.

contextual_bundling_spec.description: Optional. JSON object of contextual bundling spec for ads in Facebook contextual surfaces.

creative_sequence.description: Optional. JSON array of ad group IDs defining the sequence to show to users.

creative_diversity_data.description: Optional. JSON object of creative diversity data including scores and labels for creative variation analysis.

creative_diversity_label.description: Optional. Creative diversity label. Values: HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM.

creative_diversity_score.description: Optional. Creative diversity score (0.0-1.0) measuring variation across ad creatives.

creative_fatigue_prediction_ple.description: Optional. JSON object of creative fatigue prediction PLE data.

is_dynamic_creative_format_automation.description: Optional. Whether to use dynamic creative format automation.

is_dynamic_creative_optimization.description: Optional. Whether to use dynamic creative optimization. Deprecated in v3.2.

multi_event_conversion_attribution_windo.description: Optional. Multi-event conversion attribution window in seconds.

low_creative_reach.description: Optional. Low creative reach indicator. Values: HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM.

conversion_goal_id.description: Optional. ID of the conversion goal (CSA) as numeric string.

conversion_locations.description: Optional; usually omit, since destination_type already sets where conversions happen. Common values: WEBSITE, MOBILE_APP, WEB_AND_APP, MESSENGER, WHATSAPP, INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, PHONE_CALL, WEBSITE_AND_PHONE_CALL.

conversion_value_expression_spec.description: Optional. JSON array of conversion value expression specs.

partnership_ad_content_lists.description: Optional. JSON array of partnership ad content lists.

shops_ads_metadata_tags.description: Optional. JSON array of shops ads metadata tag integers.

is_message_marketing.description: Optional. Whether this is message marketing.

time_based_ad_rotation_id_blocks.description: Optional. JSON array of arrays of ad group IDs for time-based ad rotation.

time_based_ad_rotation_intervals.description: Optional. JSON array of UNIX timestamps defining date ranges for ad rotation.

time_start.description: Optional. Time start in ISO 8601 format or UNIX timestamp.

time_stop.description: Optional. Time stop in ISO 8601 format or UNIX timestamp.

time_suggestion.description: Optional. JSON object of suggested start/stop time for the ad set based on delivery optimization.

include_in_ad_study_cell_id.description: Optional. Ad study cell ID to include this ad set in, as numeric string.

include_in_ad_study_id.description: Optional. Ad study ID to include this ad set in, as numeric string.

lightweight_split_test_options.description: Optional. JSON object of lightweight A/B split test configuration options.

guidance_lift_estimate.description: Optional. JSON object of lift estimation for each guidance object.

brand_safety_config.description: Optional. JSON object of brand safety configuration.

breakdown_effect_eligibility.description: Optional. Whether breakdown effect is eligible.

is_lifetime_flex_with_valid_schedule.description: Optional. Whether the campaign is lifetime flex with a valid schedule.

is_sac_cfca_terms_certified.description: Optional. Whether SAC CFCA terms are certified.

metrics_metadata.description: Optional. JSON object of metrics metadata related to this ad set.

relative_value.description: Optional. Relative value weight (0.0-1.0) for multi-optimization goal balancing.

value_rule_set_id.description: Optional. Value rule set ID as numeric string.

value_rules_applied.description: Optional. Whether value rules are applied.

value_rules_spec.description: Optional. JSON object of value rules spec.

hide_ui.description: Optional. Set to true to avoid showing too many UI widgets: when creating many ad objects at once, when creating multiple levels together for the same goal (e.g. a campaign, ad set and ad in one flow), or when the user asks to hide the UI.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

scheduled_task_run.description: Send true if this conversation was started by a schedule or trigger, for example a scheduled or recurring task that runs at a set time. Send false if it was not. If you cannot tell, omit this field.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID. Format: numeric ID without "act_" prefix.

objective.description: Campaign objective. Only ODAX outcome values are accepted: OUTCOME_AWARENESS, OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT, OUTCOME_LEADS, OUTCOME_SALES, OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION. Legacy objectives (APP_INSTALLS, BRAND_AWARENESS, REACH, LEAD_GENERATION, LINK_CLICKS, VIDEO_VIEWS, etc.) are not supported and the request fails with VALIDATION. Map APP_INSTALLS to OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION.

buying_type.description: Campaign buying type. Values: AUCTION (default), RESERVED.

special_ad_categories.description: JSON array of special ad categories. Defaults to "[]". Values: NONE, EMPLOYMENT, HOUSING, FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS, ONLINE_GAMBLING_AND_GAMING. HOUSING also covers mortgages and other home loans. CREDIT is retired: use FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES for other credit, loans, insurance and financial products. Use these exact values, not display names.

campaign_bid_strategy.description: CBO ONLY. Campaign-level bid strategy. Defaults to LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP if omitted (recommended for "highest volume" or "lowest cost" strategies). Set explicitly for other strategies. Values: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, COST_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS. LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS takes its minimum ROAS from each ad set: pass bid_constraints with roas_average_floor on every ads_create_ad_set call under this campaign. Do NOT set this field for ABO — set the bid strategy on the ad set instead.

campaign_daily_budget.description: Optional. CBO ONLY. Campaign daily budget in cents. Mutually exclusive with campaign_lifetime_budget. Do NOT set this field for ABO — pass daily_budget on the subsequent ads_create_ad_set call instead.

campaign_lifetime_budget.description: Optional. CBO ONLY. Campaign lifetime budget in cents. Mutually exclusive with campaign_daily_budget. Do NOT set this field for ABO — pass lifetime_budget on the subsequent ads_create_ad_set call instead.

campaign_spend_cap.description: Optional. Maximum total spend cap for the campaign in cents.

campaign_start_time.description: Optional. Campaign start time in ISO 8601 format.

campaign_stop_time.description: Optional. Campaign stop time in ISO 8601 format.

promoted_object.description: Optional. JSON string of promoted object spec. Required for some objectives (APP_PROMOTION, LEADS, etc.). Use product_catalog_id to select a campaign catalog. This does not select product media for ads; choose media at the ad level. A published campaign catalog cannot be removed or replaced.

special_ad_category_country.description: Optional. JSON array of country codes for special ad categories. Example: ["US","CA"]. Every country targeted by an ad set's `geo_locations` must appear in this list; territories of listed countries are also allowed.

is_skadnetwork_attribution.description: Optional. Enable SKAdNetwork attribution for iOS app campaigns.

budget_schedule_specs.description: Optional. JSON array of budget schedule specs for high-demand periods.

adlabels.description: Optional. JSON array of ad label specs. Example: [{"name":"My Label"}]

campaign_optimization_type.description: Optional. Campaign optimization type. Values: NONE, ICO_ONLY.

is_using_l3_schedule.description: Optional. Whether the campaign uses L3 schedule.

iterative_split_test_configs.description: Optional. JSON array of iterative split test configuration specs.

source_campaign_id.description: Optional. The source campaign ID to copy settings from.

topline_id.description: Optional. The topline ID to associate with this campaign.

hide_ui.description: Optional. Set to true to avoid showing too many UI widgets: when creating many ad objects at once, when creating multiple levels together for the same goal (e.g. a campaign, ad set and ad in one flow), or when the user asks to hide the UI.
