scheduled_task_run.description: Send true if this conversation was started by a schedule or trigger, for example a scheduled or recurring task that runs at a set time. Send false if it was not. If you cannot tell, omit this field.

ad_account_id.description: Parent ad account ID, numeric (e.g. "123456789").

page_id.description: Facebook Page ID that will own the creative post. Required for every format except instagram_partnership_ad. For an Instagram Partnership Ad, omit this field and the tool derives the creator's Page-compatible ads identity (its linked Facebook Page or Instagram Account Backed Page); if provided, it must match that identity. For a Facebook Partnership Ad, set it to the Page publishing the ad. Must be a Page ID: if the owner is a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus creator, use their delegate Page ID, not their profile ID. If the creative is for a PROFILE_VISIT or PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT ad set, set page_id to that ad set's promoted_object.page_id; read it with ads_get_ad_entities first.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image asset. For image ads: the ad image (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For single-video ads: the video thumbnail / cover image shown before the video plays (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For PAC or MMU, put image_hash inside placement_customizations or multi_media instead. Not used for catalog carousel ads.

image_url.description: URL of an image. For image ads: the ad image (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For single-video ads: the video thumbnail / cover image shown before the video plays (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For PAC or MMU, put image_url inside placement_customizations or multi_media instead. Not used for catalog carousel ads.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video on the ad account. Required for a single-video ad, but not sufficient by itself: also provide exactly one of image_hash or image_url as the video thumbnail / cover image. For PAC or MMU, put video_id inside placement_customizations or multi_media instead. Not used for catalog carousel ads.

product_set_id.description: ID of a product set from the advertiser's catalog. Required for Advantage+ catalog carousel ads. When provided, creates a carousel creative that dynamically populates card content from the catalog at delivery time. Do not provide image_hash, image_url, or video_id when using product_set_id.

product_extensions_product_set_id.description: Product set to feature in Product Extensions (from ads_catalog_list_product_sets). Only applies when product_extensions is opted in; omit it to use the recommended set. Different from product_set_id, which creates a catalog carousel.

objective.description: Objective of the campaign this creative is for. REQUIRED when you request Product Extensions (together with conversion_location and link_url) — an explicit Product Extensions request that omits it is rejected when the tool runs the Product Extensions checks. Only these two objectives are eligible for Product Extensions; a campaign on any other objective cannot use it. Omit this field when you are not requesting Product Extensions.

conversion_location.description: Conversion location of the campaign this creative is for. REQUIRED when you request Product Extensions (together with objective and link_url) — an explicit Product Extensions request that omits it is rejected when the tool runs the Product Extensions checks. Pair PIXEL with objective OUTCOME_SALES, or WEBSITE with OUTCOME_TRAFFIC; no other pairing is eligible. Omit this field when you are not requesting Product Extensions.

link_url.description: Destination URL the creative clicks to (e.g. "https://example.com/landing"). Required for image ads, catalog carousel ads, and PAC or MMU containing an image, unless messaging_destination_type is set, which rejects link_url; optional for single-video, video-only PAC, and video-only MMU. Always include https:// scheme; if omitted the tool prepends it automatically. For catalog carousel ads, this is the default landing URL; product-specific deep links from the catalog may override it at delivery time.

display_link.description: Short URL or domain displayed on the ad (e.g. "Verizon.com"). This is presentation text, not the destination URL; put the click destination in link_url. Must be URL-shaped — a bare domain is fine, arbitrary text like "Shop now" is rejected. Supported for image, single-video, PAC, MMU, static-carousel, and Advantage+ catalog-carousel creatives. link_url is required when display_link is provided. Immutable after the creative is published. The link line that shows it is being removed from Facebook mobile Feed for single-image and single-video ads, so it may not be visible there; the response carries a warning when that applies.

message.description: One body/primary-text value shown above the image, video, or carousel. Shared across all placement_customizations entries. For a single image, a single video, or multi_media, use primary_texts instead when you want multiple variants. For carousel ads, may contain template strings like {{product.name}} filled from the catalog at delivery time.

primary_texts.description: For a single image, a single video, or multi_media: 1–5 body/primary-text variants. Meta chooses among them at delivery time. Do not combine with message; put every variant in this array. On a single image or video, the first variant is also the main text. For other creative formats, including placement_customizations, use message. On a single image or video, the variants must all differ, and two or more variants need an Awareness, Engagement, Leads or Sales objective; ads_create_ad rejects others, such as Traffic.

description.description: One short description value. Shared across all placement_customizations entries. For a single image, a single video, or multi_media, use descriptions instead when you want multiple variants. Maps to link_data.description for image ads, video_data.link_description for video ads, or template_data.description for carousel ads. Facebook Feed does not display it on single-image or single-video ads and Instagram has no description line; the response carries a warning when that applies. For video ads, also provide link_url when you set description.

descriptions.description: For a single image, a single video, or multi_media: 1–5 short-description variants. Meta chooses among them at delivery time. Do not combine with description; put every variant in this array. On a single image or video, the first variant is also the main description, so the description rules apply: on a single-video ad, also provide link_url. For other creative formats, including placement_customizations, use description. On a single image or video, the variants must all differ, and two or more variants need an Awareness, Engagement, Leads or Sales objective; ads_create_ad rejects others, such as Traffic.

call_to_action_type.description: Call-to-action button type. Defaults to LEARN_MORE if omitted. Must be an exact UPPER_CASE value from the backend CTA enum — do NOT invent or reformat a value, or the request is rejected with "call_to_action[type] must be one of the following values: …". Use one of the accepted values below; pick the one whose label matches the user's intent — do NOT guess. CTA destination is auto-set to link_url. With source_instagram_media_id, every value except NO_BUTTON requires link_url. Telephone CTAs (CALL, CALL_NOW, CALL_ME, MISSED_CALL) are not supported because they require a tel: destination, which this tool cannot supply. Use a supported CTA such as CONTACT_US, or create the telephone CTA in Ads Manager. Accepted values by category: — Shopping: SHOP_NOW (Shop Now), BUY_NOW (Buy Now), ORDER_NOW (Order Now), START_ORDER (Start Order), ADD_TO_CART (Add to Cart), SEE_SHOP (See Shop), BROWSE_SHOP (Browse Shop), VIEW_PRODUCT (View Product), BUY (Buy), SELL_NOW (Sell Now), SHOP_WITH_AI (Shop with AI). — General: LEARN_MORE (Learn More), SIGN_UP (Sign Up), OPEN_LINK (Open Link), GET_STARTED (Get Started), SEE_MORE (See More), FIND_OUT_MORE (Find Out More), VISIT_WEBSITE (Visit Website), GET_DETAILS (Get Details), CONFIRM (Confirm), NO_BUTTON (No Button). — Contact: CONTACT_US (Contact Us), CONTACT (Contact), GET_QUOTE (Get Quote), GET_A_QUOTE (Get a Quote), MESSAGE_PAGE (Message Page), WHATSAPP_MESSAGE (WhatsApp Message), INSTAGRAM_MESSAGE (Instagram Message), GET_IN_TOUCH (Get in Touch), AUDIO_CALL (Audio Call), VIDEO_CALL (Video Call), EMAIL_NOW (Email Now), ASK_A_QUESTION (Ask a Question), CHAT_NOW (Chat Now), CHAT_WITH_US (Chat with Us), ASK_FOR_MORE_INFO (Ask for More Info). — Booking: BOOK_NOW (Book Now), BOOK_TRAVEL (Book Travel), REQUEST_TIME (Request Time), MAKE_AN_APPOINTMENT (Make an Appointment), BOOK_A_CONSULTATION (Book a Consultation), GET_SHOWTIMES (Get Showtimes), BUY_TICKETS (Buy Tickets). — App: INSTALL_APP (Install App), INSTALL_MOBILE_APP (Install Mobile App), USE_APP (Use App), USE_MOBILE_APP (Use Mobile App), DOWNLOAD (Download), PLAY_GAME (Play Game), OPEN_INSTANT_APP (Open Instant App), UPDATE_APP (Update App). — Lead Gen: APPLY_NOW (Apply Now), INQUIRE_NOW (Inquire Now), GET_OFFER (Get Offer), GET_DIRECTIONS (Get Directions). — Engagement: SUBSCRIBE (Subscribe), FOLLOW_PAGE (Follow Page), EVENT_RSVP (RSVP), DONATE (Donate), DONATE_NOW (Donate Now), RAISE_MONEY (Raise Money), REFER_FRIENDS (Refer Friends). — Media: WATCH_VIDEO (Watch Video), WATCH_MORE (Watch More), LISTEN_NOW (Listen Now), LISTEN_MUSIC (Listen Music), WATCH_LIVE_VIDEO (Watch Live Video).

name.description: Name of this ad creative as seen in the ad account's library. Strongly recommended.

headline.description: One short headline shown under the image (link_data.name), video (video_data.title), or carousel cards (template_data.name). Shared across all placement_customizations entries. For a single image, a single video, or multi_media, use headlines instead when you want multiple variants.

headlines.description: For a single image, a single video, or multi_media: 1–5 headline variants. Meta chooses among them at delivery time. Do not combine with headline; put every variant in this array. On a single image or video, the first variant is also the main headline. For other creative formats, including placement_customizations, use headline. On a single image or video, the variants must all differ, and two or more variants need an Awareness, Engagement, Leads or Sales objective; ads_create_ad rejects others, such as Traffic.

instagram_user_id.description: Instagram User (IG Business Account) ID for IG placement delivery. For instagram_partnership_ad this is required and identifies the creator; it accepts a numeric account ID, username, @handle, or Instagram profile URL, resolves it to a professional account, and derives page_id from the creator's linked Facebook Page or Instagram Account Backed Page. With source_instagram_media_id this is required and names the account that owns the post. For other formats, pass the numeric id returned by ads_get_ig_accounts or instagram_user_id from an existing valid ad; it is required when the ad will deliver on Instagram placements, including Advantage+ placements.

url_tags.description: URL parameters appended to every destination link of the creative, as a query string without a leading "?", for example "utm_source=meta&utm_medium=paid_social&utm_campaign={{campaign.name}}". Ads Manager calls this URL parameters. Set it here when the advertiser tracks clicks; it cannot be added after the creative is created. Enabled per calling app while it rolls out; where it is not, the request is rejected and nothing is created (see URL parameters and instant forms in the tool description).

lead_gen_form_id.description: ID of an existing instant form (lead form) owned by page_id. The button then opens that form instead of a website, for an ad set that optimizes for leads on the ad (OUTCOME_LEADS campaign, destination_type ON_AD). Single-image and single-video creatives only, and not with messaging_destination_type. call_to_action_type must be one that can open a form: LEARN_MORE (the default when omitted), SIGN_UP, APPLY_NOW, GET_QUOTE, GET_OFFER, SUBSCRIBE, DOWNLOAD, CONTACT, GET_IN_TOUCH or BOOK_TRAVEL; any other value is rejected. link_url is optional here; when omitted, the tool uses the placeholder link Ads Manager uses for instant-form ads. The Page must have accepted the Lead Ads Terms of Service. Enabled per calling app while it rolls out; where it is not, the request is rejected and nothing is created (see URL parameters and instant forms in the tool description).

self_ai_disclosure.description: AI-generated content disclosure for the creative. Set to "OPT_IN" to declare that this creative contains media created or edited with a third-party generative AI tool; set to "OPT_OUT" to declare it does not. Omit if unknown. Only these two exact UPPER_CASE values are accepted. When you opt in, Meta may display an "AI info" label on the ad; whether it appears depends on the regions the ad is delivered to and their AI-transparency requirements. Decide this before creating the creative — no update tool can set it afterwards. Always list this field for the advertiser so they can decide; disclosure is their responsibility, so never set or infer a value on their behalf. The declaration takes effect only where AI-transparency rules require it — currently the European Region, India, Taiwan, California, and New York.

object_story_id.description: ID of an existing organic Page post to boost, as {page_id}_{post_id} (e.g. "1234567890_9876543210"). The embedded page must match page_id. Both halves must be canonical IDs: {page_id} is a Page ID (for a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus creator, their delegate Page ID — not their profile ID), and {post_id} is the post's own ID — not the ID of a photo, video, or other attachment on it. The post must still exist, be published, belong to that Page, and be visible/promotable by the caller; retrying a deleted, unpublished, or inaccessible post cannot repair it. For an ad set optimized for link clicks, the post must already contain a valid external destination and CTA because existing-post copy and CTA cannot be added here. The post media and copy are used as-is, so do NOT combine this with image_hash, image_url, video_id, placement_customizations, placement_videos, product_set_id, cards, link_url, message, primary_texts, description, descriptions, headline, headlines, call_to_action_type, or display_link. instagram_user_id may be provided for Instagram placement delivery.

source_instagram_media_id.description: Media ID of an existing organic Instagram post to promote: an id returned by ads_get_ig_media for the account in instagram_user_id, which is required alongside it. page_id must be the Facebook Page linked to that account. Ad media, such as a boosted copy or the effective Instagram media ID read from an existing creative, is rejected. The post media and caption are used as-is, so do NOT combine this with object_story_id, image_hash, image_url, video_id, placement_customizations, placement_videos, multi_media, product_set_id, cards, message, primary_texts, description, descriptions, headline, headlines, display_link, or a Partnership Ad. link_url optionally adds a button; call_to_action_type picks its label. Every call_to_action_type other than NO_BUTTON requires link_url. Without a link, use NO_BUTTON or omit call_to_action_type.

advantage_plus_creative.description: Turn on Advantage+ Creative — Meta's automatic per-impression creative optimizations (image brightness/contrast, text improvements, and similar). This is the master toggle most callers want. Set true to enable it. Set false to leave the master feature off; false does not override a supplied degrees_of_freedom_spec, and does not turn off the default enhancements; use advantage_plus_creative_defaults=OFF for that. Only set true when the advertiser wants Meta to automatically optimize the creative.

advantage_plus_creative_features.description: Specific Advantage+ Creative feature names to opt the creative into individually. Each entry must be an exact lower_snake_case feature name (e.g. "image_touchups", "text_optimizations", "image_animation"). Most callers only need advantage_plus_creative; use this only when the advertiser asks for specific enhancements.

degrees_of_freedom_spec.description: Raw Marketing API degrees_of_freedom_spec, passed as a JSON-ENCODED STRING (NOT a nested JSON object) — e.g. "{\"creative_features_spec\":{\"text_optimizations\":{\"enroll_status\":\"OPT_OUT\"}}}". Use only for what the advantage_plus_creative / advantage_plus_creative_features shortcuts cannot express: opting a feature OUT, or per-feature customizations. Do not combine it with advantage_plus_creative=true or a non-empty advantage_plus_creative_features list. It may be combined with advantage_plus_creative=false while preserving the raw spec. standard_enhancements is retired: OPT_OUT is ignored and OPT_IN is rejected; set individual features instead.

cards.description: Cards for a STATIC carousel ad (2–10). Distinct from Advantage+ catalog carousel: do NOT combine cards with product_set_id, image_hash, image_url, video_id, placement_customizations, placement_videos, or multi_media. Each card needs exactly one image (image_hash or image_url); a video card sets video_id and may omit the image, in which case the video's default thumbnail is used. Top-level link_url and call_to_action_type act as per-card fallbacks.

items.description: A single static carousel card.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image for this card. Provide exactly one of image_hash or image_url. Required for an image card; optional for a video card (used as the thumbnail, otherwise the video's default thumbnail is used).

image_url.description: URL of the image for this card. Provide exactly one of image_hash or image_url. Required for an image card; optional for a video card (used as the thumbnail, otherwise the video's default thumbnail is used).

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video for this card (makes it a video card). A thumbnail is optional: if you omit image_hash/image_url, the video's default thumbnail is used automatically.

link.description: Destination URL for this card. Falls back to the top-level link_url when omitted; https:// is prepended if missing. Required for image cards (via card link or the top-level fallback); optional for video cards.

headline.description: Short headline shown on this card (child_attachments.name). Alias: name.

name.description: Alias for headline (matches ads_get_creatives output). Used only when headline is not set.

description.description: Description text shown on this card (child_attachments.description).

call_to_action_type.description: Per-card CTA button type (same accepted values as the top-level call_to_action_type). Falls back to the top-level call_to_action_type.

placement_customizations.description: Placement Asset Customization (2–10 assets). Each entry contains exactly one of image_hash, image_url, or video_id. Exactly one entry is the fallback and contains no placement fields. Other entries need non-empty publisher_platforms; placement rules and media assets may not repeat or overlap. When one asset serves multiple platforms, combine those platforms and their positions in one entry instead of repeating the asset in separate entries. Never reuse an override asset as the fallback. If the request has no fallback, ask for one and do not call the tool. Do not combine with multi_media, placement_videos, or top-level media fields.

items.description: One image or video and the non-overlapping placements where it should be used.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image in this ad account. Provide exactly one of image_hash, image_url, or video_id.

image_url.description: Absolute http/https image URL. The tool downloads it into this ad account and uses the resulting image hash. Provide exactly one media field.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video. It must be accessible and fully processed (ready). Provide exactly one media field.

publisher_platforms.description: Platforms for this asset: facebook, instagram, messenger, audience_network, threads, whatsapp, or oculus. Omit this and all position fields on exactly one entry to make it the fallback asset.

facebook_positions.description: Optional Facebook positions, such as feed, story, facebook_reels, marketplace, instream_video, or right_hand_column. Requires facebook in publisher_platforms.

instagram_positions.description: Optional Instagram positions: stream, story, reels, explore, explore_home, profile_feed, profile_reels, ig_search, reels_overlay, or shop. Requires instagram in publisher_platforms.

messenger_positions.description: Optional Messenger positions: sponsored_messages, messenger_home, story, or marketing_messages. Requires messenger in publisher_platforms.

audience_network_positions.description: Optional Audience Network positions: classic, instream_video, rewarded_video, or ctv_instream_video. Requires audience_network in publisher_platforms.

threads_positions.description: Optional Threads positions: threads_stream. Requires threads in publisher_platforms.

whatsapp_positions.description: Optional WhatsApp positions: status, marketing_messages, channel, or smb_marketing_messages. Requires whatsapp in publisher_platforms.

multi_media.description: Multi-media optimization (MMU) asset pool with 2–10 unique images, videos, or both. Meta chooses which eligible asset to deliver. Pair it with primary_texts, headlines, and descriptions for up to five variants of each; use the singular message, headline, and description fields only when you want one value. This field does not set exact placement rules or a fallback; use placement_customizations for that. Do not combine with placement_customizations, placement_videos, top-level media, product_set_id, cards, object_story_id, or facebook_partnership_ad.

items.description: One image or video in the delivery-optimized MMU asset pool.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image in this ad account. Provide exactly one of image_hash, image_url, or video_id.

image_url.description: Absolute http/https image URL. The tool downloads it into this ad account and uses the resulting image hash. Provide exactly one media field.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video. It must be accessible and fully processed. The tool uses its default thumbnail. Provide exactly one media field.

placement_videos.description: Legacy video-only Placement Asset Customization input (2–10). New calls should use placement_customizations. Exactly one entry must be a fallback that contains only video_id. Other entries require non-empty publisher_platforms. Rules and videos may not repeat or overlap. Do not combine with placement_customizations, multi_media, or top-level media fields.

items.description: A pre-uploaded video and the placements where it should be used.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video on the ad account.

publisher_platforms.description: Platforms for this video: facebook, instagram, messenger, audience_network, threads, whatsapp, or oculus. Omit this and all position fields on exactly one entry to make it the fallback video.

facebook_positions.description: Optional Facebook positions, such as feed, story, facebook_reels, marketplace, instream_video, or right_hand_column. Requires facebook in publisher_platforms.

instagram_positions.description: Optional Instagram positions: stream, story, reels, explore, explore_home, profile_feed, profile_reels, ig_search, reels_overlay, or shop. Requires instagram in publisher_platforms.

messenger_positions.description: Optional Messenger positions: sponsored_messages, messenger_home, story, or marketing_messages. Requires messenger in publisher_platforms.

audience_network_positions.description: Optional Audience Network positions: classic, instream_video, rewarded_video, or ctv_instream_video. Requires audience_network in publisher_platforms.

threads_positions.description: Optional Threads positions: threads_stream. Requires threads in publisher_platforms.

whatsapp_positions.description: Optional WhatsApp positions: status, marketing_messages, channel, or smb_marketing_messages. Requires whatsapp in publisher_platforms.

facebook_partnership_ad.description: Facebook Partnership Ad (branded content) created from an existing post — via an ad code (facebook_boost_post_access_token) or by referencing the post directly (object_story_id). Provide this object to create a Partnership Ad — do NOT also provide image_hash, image_url, video_id, multi_media, product_set_id, or cards. To build a new Instagram Partnership Ad creative from media instead, use instagram_partnership_ad; to boost a creator's existing Instagram post, use ads_boost_ig_post.

facebook_boost_post_access_token.description: Encrypted ad code (a.k.a. "boost post access token") that a Facebook creator generated to authorize this advertiser to boost one of the creator's existing Facebook posts as a Facebook Partnership Ad. Provide exactly one of facebook_boost_post_access_token or object_story_id.

object_story_id.description: Reference to an existing Facebook branded-content post to boost, formatted "<post_owner_page_id>_<post_id>". The page half is the Page ID of the post's owner (for a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus owner, their delegate Page ID, not their profile ID); the post half must be the post's own ID, not the ID of an attachment on it. Use when the advertiser already has permission on the post (instead of an ad code). Provide exactly one of facebook_boost_post_access_token or object_story_id.

ad_format.description: Partnership Ad header format, as an integer. Optional; omit it unless the advertiser asked for a specific header, in which case: 1 = dual header (both identities, the default), 2 = single header, 3 = dynamic (optimized at delivery).

sponsor_page_id.description: REQUIRED. Facebook Page ID of the Partnership Ad's secondary identity (the boosted post's owner is the primary). In a sponsor boost it is the Page publishing the ad, the same value as page_id; in a creator boost it is the partner Page. Must be a Page ID — for a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus partner, their delegate Page ID, not their profile ID.

instagram_partnership_ad.description: Instagram Partnership Ad (branded content) built from new media in this same call. Unlike facebook_partnership_ad, this one DOES carry media — supply image_hash, image_url, video_id or cards as usual. Set instagram_user_id to the CREATOR's numeric account ID, username, @handle, or Instagram profile URL; page_id is derived from the resolved creator's linked Facebook Page or Instagram Account Backed Page unless that matching identity ID is provided. The two fields here name the sponsoring brand. To promote a post the creator has already published, use ads_boost_ig_post instead — this object is for a new creative only, and cannot be combined with object_story_id.

sponsor_instagram_user_id.description: REQUIRED. Instagram account ID of the sponsoring brand. This is what distinguishes an Instagram Partnership Ad from a Facebook one, so it must be the brand and never the creator — the creator goes in the top-level instagram_user_id.

sponsor_page_id.description: REQUIRED. Facebook Page ID of the same sponsoring brand. Both sponsor fields are required together: supplying only one leaves the brand half-identified and the ad would be created as an ordinary one.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

scheduled_task_run.description: Send true if this conversation was started by a schedule or trigger, for example a scheduled or recurring task that runs at a set time. Send false if it was not. If you cannot tell, omit this field.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID. Format: numeric ID without "act_" prefix.

subtype.description: The type of custom audience to create. Values: CUSTOM (customer list / DFCA — requires customer_file_source), WEBSITE (WCA — requires rule with pixel event_sources), ENGAGEMENT (ECA — requires rule with ig_business/page/shopping_page/shopping_ig/marketplace_listings/lead/ig_lead_generation/canvas event_sources), MOBILE_APP (MACA — requires rule with app event_sources), LOOKALIKE (LAL — requires origin_audience_id and lookalike_ratio; origin must NOT itself be a LOOKALIKE).

origin_audience_id.description: Required for LOOKALIKE subtype only. The numeric ID of an existing custom audience to model this lookalike on, passed as a string. The origin can be CUSTOM (DFCA), WEBSITE (WCA), ENGAGEMENT (ECA), or MOBILE_APP (MACA), but NOT another LOOKALIKE. Ignored for non-LOOKALIKE subtypes.

lookalike_ratio.description: Required for LOOKALIKE subtype only. The share of the population to match. Range: 0.01 (1%, closest match, smallest audience) to 0.20 (20%, broadest, largest audience). Default: 0.01 (1%). Ignored for non-LOOKALIKE subtypes. DO NOT ask the user for a country — geography is handled automatically (allow_international_seeds=true).

customer_file_source.description: Required for CUSTOM subtype only. How the customer data was sourced. Values: USER_PROVIDED_ONLY (advertiser collected directly), PARTNER_PROVIDED_ONLY (from a partner), BOTH_USER_AND_PARTNER_PROVIDED (mixed sources). Ignored for WEBSITE subtype.

rule.description: Required for WEBSITE, ENGAGEMENT, and MOBILE_APP subtypes. MUST be a JSON-encoded string, NOT a raw JSON object. Pass the rule as a single string value like "{\"inclusions\":{...}}", not as a nested object. Top-level structure: {"inclusions":{...}, "exclusions":{...}}. "exclusions" is optional. Each block has: {"operator":"or","rules":[<rule1>, <rule2>, ...]}. Each rule has: {"event_sources":[{"type":"<TYPE>","id":"<ID>"}], "retention_seconds":<SECONDS>, "filter":{"operator":"and","filters":[...]}, "template":"<TEMPLATE>"}. For WEBSITE: event_sources type must be "pixel". Template is REQUIRED. Three targeting flows: (1) All visitors: template "ALL_VISITORS", filter {"field":"url","operator":"i_contains","value":""} (empty value matches all). CRITICAL: do NOT use event/PageView for all visitors — use url/i_contains with empty value. (2) Specific pages: template "VISITORS_BY_URL", filter {"field":"url","operator":"i_contains","value":"<keyword>"}. (3) Time spent: template "TOP_TIME_SPENDERS", aggregation {"type":"time_spent","method":"percentile","operator":"in_range","value":{"from":75,"to":100}}. Standard/custom events: template "VISITORS_BY_URL", filter {"field":"event","operator":"eq","value":"Purchase"/"AddToCart"/"Lead"/etc}. For MOBILE_APP (MACA): event_sources type must be "app". Templates: "MACA_APP_LAUNCHED_USERS" for app launchers (event "fb_mobile_activate_app", NO aggregation); "MACA_MOST_ACTIVE_USERS" for top app users by event count (event "fb_mobile_activate_app" with aggregation {"type":"count","method":"percentile","operator":"in_range","value":{"from":<95|90|75>,"to":100}}); "MACA_TOP_PURCHASE_USERS" for top spenders (event "fb_mobile_purchase" with aggregation {"type":"sum","field":"_valueToSumInUSD","method":"percentile","operator":"in_range","value":{"from":<95|90|75>,"to":100}}). Both percentile-based templates only support top 5%, 10%, 25% windows. Template is OPTIONAL for custom advertiser-defined events; the event name comes from the advertiser (ask the user) and must not be invented. Ignored for CUSTOM and LOOKALIKE subtypes.

prefill.description: Optional. For WEBSITE, ENGAGEMENT, and MOBILE_APP subtypes. Whether to backfill the audience with historical data. Default: true. Ignored for CUSTOM and LOOKALIKE subtypes.

audience_labels.description: Optional. For CUSTOM, WEBSITE, ENGAGEMENT, and MOBILE_APP subtypes. A single label describing this audience. Labels help find audiences for ads more effectively. Engaged audiences: "qualified_leads", "disqualified_leads", "app_installers", "trial_users", "engaged_users". Customers: "high_value_customers", "low_value_customers", "at_risk", "disengaged", "customer_leads". Ignored for LOOKALIKE subtype.

is_value_based.description: Optional. For CUSTOM subtype only. Set to true to create a value-based audience for use with value optimization. Default: false. Ignored for WEBSITE subtype.

retention_days.description: Optional. For CUSTOM subtype only. Number of days to retain audience members. Range: 1-180. Default: 180. For WEBSITE, retention is set via retention_seconds in the rule JSON.

file_name.description: The local file name, exactly as on disk.

mime_type.description: One of image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, video/mp4 or video/quicktime.

file_size.description: The exact file size in bytes: images up to 30 MiB and videos up to 100 MiB.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account the file is for (numeric, without the "act_" prefix). Only needed when the goal is to create an ad creative; skip it when uploading a file for catalog updates.

creative_id.description: The numeric ID of the ad creative to delete (e.g. "123456789").

ad_account_id.description: Optional ad account context, numeric with or without the "act_" prefix. If provided, it must own the creative. The creative_id is sufficient when the account is unknown.

Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

scheduled_task_run.description: Send true if this conversation was started by a schedule or trigger, for example a scheduled or recurring task that runs at a set time. Send false if it was not. If you cannot tell, omit this field.

analysis_level.description:
The granularity level for insights computation. Determines whether results are grouped by campaign, ad set, or individual ad.

  VALID VALUES: Only values supported by the specific tool are accepted (see per-tool matrix below). Passing an unsupported value returns empty results with no error.

  DETERMINING WHICH VALUE(S) TO USE — apply rules in order, stop at FIRST match (all keyword matching is case-insensitive):

    RULE A — Single-level tool: Tool supports only ONE level → use that level. 1 call.

    RULE B — Full-hierarchy + "campaign": Tool supports AD, ADSET, AND CAMPAIGN, and query contains "campaign" or "campaigns" → 3 calls in order: CAMPAIGN, ADSET, AD.

    RULE C — AD+ADSET tool + "adset": Tool supports both AD and ADSET, and query contains "adset", "adsets", "ad set", or "ad sets" → 2 calls in order: ADSET, AD.

    RULE D — Standalone "ad": Query contains "ad" or "ads" as a separate word → 1 call: AD.
      STANDALONE means separated by spaces, punctuation, or boundaries — not embedded in another word.
      ✓ Matches: "ad performance", "my ads", "improve ad CPR", "best ad"
      ✗ Does NOT match: "adset", "ad set", "ad sets", "advertisement", "advertiser"

    RULE E — Default: No keyword matched → 1 call for EACH supported level (highest to lowest).

  CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:
    - NEVER pass a value not in the tool's supported levels — if a matched rule produces a level the tool does not support, skip that level
    - If skipping unsupported levels results in zero calls for a tool, do not call that tool with analysis_level
    - ALWAYS make SEPARATE tool calls per level — never combine multiple levels in one call
    - ALWAYS evaluate rules A → B → C → D → E in order; use the FIRST that matches
  Valid values: AD, ADSET

items.description: Entity ID

analysis_metric.description:
If the user query mentions a specific KPI metric (e.g., ROAS, CPC, conversion
          rate, impressions), extract it and check against the valid values listed below. 
  CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:
    -  Only include analysis_metric if the user explicitly named a metric
    -  If yes AND it matches with the valid values provided below → provide analysis_metric with that value
    -  If no metric mentioned in query → DO NOT provide analysis_metric
  CRITICAL INVARIANT: 
   - Use ONLY the valid values listed below

  Valid values: CPR, CTR, CPM, CPC, ROAS

date_preset.description:
Preset date range for computing insights. Use ONLY when date range matches the valid values below.

  CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:
   - Extract preset from user query and EXACT match against the valid values listed below
   - ONLY use the EXACT preset value as listed below in valid values — do NOT shorten, abbreviate, or infer variations
   - If no EXACT match found in query → do NOT use date_preset

   - All valid values are lowercase with underscores: last_7d, this_month etc.
  CRITICAL INVARIANT:
    - Cannot be combined with date_from and date_to
  .  - MUST be one of the valid values listed below

  Valid values: today, yesterday, last_2_days, last_7d, last_14d, last_28d, last_30d, this_week, last_week, this_month, last_month, lifetime

date_from.description:
Start date for insights computation in Advertiser's timezone (YYYY-MM-DD format)
  CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:
    - Use this ONLY when the user specifies a custom date range that does NOT match any preset (e.g., 'from March 1
        to March 15', 'between these two specific dates')
  CRITICAL INVARIANTS:
    -  MUST be in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., 2024-03-15)
    -  Cannot be combined with date_preset
    -  MUST be used together with date_to (both required if either is provided)

date_to.description:
End date for insights computation in Advertiser's timezone (YYYY-MM-DD format)
  Use this ONLY when the user specifies a custom date range that does NOT match any preset
   CRITICAL INVARIANTS:
    -  MUST be in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., 2024-03-31)
    -  Cannot be combined with date_preset
    -  MUST be used together with date_from (both required if either is provided)
    -  date_to MUST be on or after date_from

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

asset_id.description: The product catalog to read access for. Format: Numeric. Example: '1234567890'.

user_type.description: Omit to list people (employees and system users). Combined with user_id set to a partner business ID, returns one row checking that partner: access_status HAS_ACCESS, NOT_A_PARTNER, REQUEST_PENDING, BUSINESS_HAS_NO_ACCESS_TO_ASSET (a partner with no share) or NO_PERMISSIONS_GRANTED, and reason naming the fix. Partner listing and checks require partner-management permission on the catalog's owning business. EMPLOYEE and SYSTEM_USER are not supported here yet.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring of an assigned user display name. With user_type=AGENCY, all-digit input matches an exact partner business ID and other text a partner business-name substring. Omit or pass an empty string for the full visible assignment list. Cannot be combined with user_id. Does not search email.

On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

scheduled_task_run.description: Send true if this conversation was started by a schedule or trigger, for example a scheduled or recurring task that runs at a set time. Send false if it was not. If you cannot tell, omit this field.

after_answer_offer_report.description: Do not send this field. If your answer analyzes the performance, results, creative or plans of one or more Meta ad accounts, and your advertiser_job is report_measure_or_look_up, assess_and_optimize_performance, explain_poor_results, creative_insights_and_ideas or plan_future_campaigns (or you sent none), call the offer_report tool with only Meta ad account IDs you analyzed in ad_account_ids and the same advertiser_job, after all other tool results are back. Do this after each new analysis, including follow-up analyses in the same conversation and cross-platform analyses that include Meta ad accounts, even if offer_report ran earlier. This is required even for a one-time question. Load offer_report first if needed (for example, with tool search). Do not call it during a scheduled task.

asset_id.description: The product catalog whose assignment to set. Format: Numeric.

recipient_id.description: Who the change is for, as in the confirmed preview: a person's business-scoped user ID, or a partner business's ID. Not a personal Facebook user ID.

permissions.description: The complete confirmed permission set. Enum values are possible inputs, not universally grantable: newly added permissions must come from the selected catalog/business available_permissions. Existing nonselectable named permissions may be retained. Replaces the user's current permissions on the asset. An empty list removes all of their direct access.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

audience_labels.description: Optional. A single label describing this audience. Applies to both DFCA (REGULAR) and WCA (PLATFORM) audiences. Labels help find audiences for ads more effectively.

A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

scheduled_task_run.description: Send true if this conversation was started by a schedule or trigger, for example a scheduled or recurring task that runs at a set time. Send false if it was not. If you cannot tell, omit this field.

ad_account_id.description: MUST be the ad account that actually owns the entity. The update is rejected with error_category=VALIDATION when the supplied ID does not match the entity's true owner.

entity_id.description: The complete numeric ID of the campaign, ad set, or ad returned by ads_get_ad_entities. Do not use a name, placeholder, multiple IDs, or a suffixed ID. Correct an invalid ID instead of retrying it unchanged.

entity_type.description: Type of entity to update. Values: campaign, ad_set, ad.

fields.description: Required unless discard_draft_changes is true, in which case omit it: sending fields with discard_draft_changes is rejected with error_category=VALIDATION. JSON-encoded object of Ads API field names to new values. Do not send null, a number, a boolean, a JSON string value, or a non-empty array. For an empty update, use {}. Use the field names from the tool description, NOT the argument names of the ads_create_* tools: a campaign budget is daily_budget / lifetime_budget and a rename is name. Unrecognized field names are rejected, and an ad's creative or creative_id cannot be set here; to turn Advantage+ creative enhancements on or off for an ad, use the advantage_plus_creative_* fields described in the tool description instead. Budget fields (daily_budget, lifetime_budget) must be integers in the ad account currency's minor unit (e.g. cents), so a $50.00 daily budget is 5000. Example: {"name":"New Name","daily_budget":5000}. For a campaign, only set objective if the user explicitly asks to change it, and only to an ODAX outcome (OUTCOME_AWARENESS, OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT, OUTCOME_LEADS, OUTCOME_SALES, OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION); legacy objectives (LINK_CLICKS, APP_INSTALLS, CONVERSIONS, REACH, etc.) are rejected with error_category=VALIDATION.

advantage_audience_off_reason.description: When you send `targeting_automation.advantage_audience` = 0, the advertiser-side reason from the tool description that applies: ADVERTISER_REQUESTED_OFF (1), HARD_AGE_REQUIREMENT (2), CUSTOM_AUDIENCE_ONLY (3) or ADVANTAGE_AUDIENCE_UNAVAILABLE (4).

discard_draft_changes.description: Optional. Set to true to discard the entity's pending draft changes instead of editing it. Omit fields: combining the two is rejected with error_category=VALIDATION and nothing is discarded. Without confirmation_token this only previews: nothing is deleted, and the response lists every object that would be removed in discard_preview plus a confirmation_token. Show that list to the user, get explicit confirmation, then call again with the token to discard.

confirmation_token.description: Only with discard_draft_changes. The confirmation_token from the preview the user confirmed. If the draft changed since that preview, the call is rejected with error_category=VALIDATION and nothing is discarded; preview again.

hide_ui.description: Optional. Set to true when updating budgets on multiple campaigns or ad sets at once, to avoid showing a budget preview widget for each update, or when the user asks to hide the UI.
